- When sentiment is high (≥0.6) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment is low (≤0.4) and forecast is overly conservative, slightly increase the mid-range to avoid underestimating rebound.  
- Forecast errors often occur in the 10–15th day of the 30-day horizon — adjust early in the forecast window to align with mean reversion patterns.  
- If the last 3–5 days of history show strong downward momentum, the model tends to underestimate the rebound — add 2–5% to the forecast from day 10 onward.  
- When sentiment is volatile (fluctuating between 0.3–0.7), avoid smooth extrapolation — use a 3-day moving average of sentiment to weight forecast adjustments.  
- Overshoots after spikes (especially >65) are common — cap forecast at 65–68 unless sentiment confirms strong bullish momentum.  
- If true outcome is consistently 2–3% higher than forecast, apply a 1–2% upward bias adjustment for the next 5-day window.
